contract_reproduction.exact_contract: R-01 through R-16 remain mapped to exact PLAN clauses, the sole §20 roadmap, validation, and human gates. PLAN §§2, 9, 10.1, 14, 15, and 17 cover install; ideation and research; typed decisions; exact-digest READY; admission; isolated execution; review; merge and Effect reconciliation; observation; rollback; cleanup; consumer release; export; and uninstall. The Issue/CLI surface remains an explicitly future contract with session-derived identity, displayed digest/diff, durable typed event/receipt, wait/error response, replay behavior, and retention/export rules.

Protected Git, authenticated human issuance, approval custody, the purpose-only PolicyAdmissionReceipt issuer, runtime validation, narrow actuators, durable facts, external resources, and disposable workers remain separate authorities. Bounded delegation applies only to closed R0/R1 profiles after every human-needed predicate is false. R2-R4, exception, UNKNOWN, canary, widening, promotion, cleanup-risk, quiescence, and break-glass decisions remain human controlled. Tenant plus typed ScopeRef identity, signed context, purpose-bound approvals, restricted database roles, total sandbox selection, capability intersection, supply-chain pins, and non-waivable break-glass boundaries fail closed.

PLAN §20 remains the sole increment-numbering authority. Release 0 is one-owner/one-repository, read-only, credential-free, restartable, repair-receipted, and exportable. External writers wait for Increment 3 PostgreSQL restricted-role, CAS/outbox, database-time lease, restore/replay, and real two-session race proof. A second repository waits for FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or stronger isolation, substitution tests, and Increment 8. Reviews bind exact heads and expire on change; auto-merge remains off through Release 0 and the draft-PR pilot, then is limited to one earned closed R1 profile.

Consumer releases inventory, pin, and rehash managed inputs and outputs, and produce verification or rollback receipts through self-test, isolated dogfood, and opt-in rings. Cross-boundary transfer requires a dual-owner, purpose- and field-limited, expiring, revocable envelope and receipt. Engineering remains first. GTM begins only after engineering admission as proposal/read-only research with a named owner; publication, spend, and contact remain human-gated.
